subclasses.name: Berserker
description: For some barbarians, rage is a means to an end--that end being violence. The Path of the Berserker is a path of untrammeled fury, slick with blood. As you enter the berserker's rage, you thrill in the chaos of battle, heedless of your own health or well-being.

features.name: Frenzy
description: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).

features.name: Mindless Rage
description: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
description: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.
If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

features.name: Retaliation
description: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Champion
description: The archetypal Champion focuses on the development of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Those who model themselves on this archetype combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

features.name: Improved Critical
description: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

features.name: Remarkable Athlete
description: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.

features.name: Additional Fighting Style
description: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

features.name: Superior Critical
description: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

features.name: Survivor
description: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Devotion
description: The Oath of Devotion binds a paladin to the loftiest ideals of justice, virtue, and order. Sometimes called cavaliers, white knights, or holy warriors, these paladins meet the ideal of the knight in shining armor, acting with honor in pursuit of justice and the greater good. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some, for better or worse, hold the rest of the world to the same standards. Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods' tenets as the measure of their devotion. They hold angels--the perfect servants of good--as their ideals, and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Sacred Weapon
description: As an action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with positive energy, using your Channel Divinity. For 1 minute, you add your Charisma modifier to attack rolls made with that weapon (with a minimum bonus of +1). The weapon also emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light 20 feet beyond that. If the weapon is not already magical, it becomes magical for the duration.
You can end this effect on your turn as part of any other action. If you are no longer holding or carrying this weapon, or if you fall unconscious, this effect ends.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Unholy
description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring fiends and undead, using your Channel Divinity. Each fiend or undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can't willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can't take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there's nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

features.name: Aura of Devotion
description: Starting at 7th level, you and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can't be charmed while you are conscious.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

features.name: Purity of Spirit
description: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.

features.name: Holy Nimbus
description: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.

subclasses.name: Draconic
description: Your innate magic comes from draconic magic that was mingled with your blood or that of your ancestors. Most often, sorcerers with this origin trace their descent back to a mighty sorcerer of ancient times who made a bargain with a dragon or who might even have claimed a dragon parent. Some of these bloodlines are well established in the world, but most are obscure. Any given sorcerer could be the first of a new bloodline, as a result of a pact or some other exceptional circumstance.

features.name: Dragon Ancestor
description: At 1st level, you choose one type of dragon as your ancestor. The damage type associated with each dragon is used by features you gain later.
You can speak, read, and write Draconic. Additionally, whenever you make a Charisma check when interacting with dragons, your proficiency bonus is doubled if it applies to the check.

features.name: Draconic Resilience
description: As magic flows through your body, it causes physical traits of your dragon ancestors to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen of dragon-like scales. When you aren't wearing armor, your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Elemental Affinity
description: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a spell that deals damage of the type associated with your draconic ancestry, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. At the same time, you can spend 1 sorcery point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

features.name: Dragon Wings
description: At 14th level, you gain the ability to sprout a pair of dragon wings from your back, gaining a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can create these wings as a bonus action on your turn. They last until you dismiss them as a bonus action on your turn.
You can't manifest your wings while wearing armor unless the armor is made to accommodate them, and clothing not made to accommodate your wings might be destroyed when you manifest them.

features.name: Draconic Presence
description: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

subclasses.name: Evocation
description: You focus your study on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast enemy armies from afar. Others use their spectacular power to protect the weak, while some seek their own gain as bandits, adventurers, or aspiring tyrants.

features.name: Evocation Savant
description: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
description: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
description: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Empowered Evocation
description: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

features.name: Overchannel
description: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

subclasses.name: Fiend
description: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.

features.name: Dark One's Blessing
description: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).

features.name: Dark One's Own Luck
description: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Fiendish Resilience
description: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

features.name: Hurl Through Hell
description: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.

At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Hunter
description: Emulating the Hunter archetype means accepting your place as a bulwark between civilization and the terrors of the wilderness. As you walk the Hunter's path, you learn specialized techniques for fighting the threats you face, from rampaging ogres and hordes of orcs to towering giants and terrifying dragons.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
description: At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Colossus Slayer
Giant Killer
Horde Breaker

features.name: Defensive Tactics
description: At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Escape the Horde
Multiattack Defense
Steel Will

features.name: Multiattack
description: At 11th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Volley
Whirlwind Attack

features.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
description: At 15th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Evasion
Stand Against the Tide
Uncanny Dodge

subclasses.name: Land
description: The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
description: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Natural Recovery
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.

features.name: Land's Stride
description: Starting at 6th level, moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.
In addition, you have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such those created by the entangle spell.

features.name: Nature's Ward
description: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

features.name: Nature's Sanctuary
description: When you reach 14th level, creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. The creature is aware of this effect before it makes its attack against you.

subclasses.name: Life
description: The Life domain focuses on the vibrant positive energy--one of the fundamental forces of the universe--that sustains all life. The gods of life promote vitality and health through healing the sick and wounded, caring for those in need, and driving away the forces of death and undeath. Almost any non-evil deity can claim influence over this domain, particularly agricultural deities, sun gods, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community.

features.name: Bonus Proficiency
description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

features.name: Disciple of Life
description: Also starting at 1st level, your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to heal the badly injured.
As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that can restore a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level.

Choose any creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide those hit points among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half of its hit point maximum. You can't use this feature on an undead or a construct.

features.name: Blessed Healer
description: Beginning at 6th level, the healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with divine energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

features.name: Supreme Healing
description: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

subclasses.name: Lore
description: Bards of the College of Lore know something about most things, collecting bits of knowledge from sources as diverse as scholarly tomes and peasant tales. Whether singing folk ballads in taverns or elaborate compositions in royal courts, these bards use their gifts to hold audiences spellbound. When the applause dies down, the audience members might find themselves questioning everything they held to be true, from their faith in the priesthood of the local temple to their loyalty to the king. The loyalty of these bards lies in the pursuit of beauty and truth, not in fealty to a monarch or following the tenets of a deity. A noble who keeps such a bard as a herald or advisor knows that the bard would rather be honest than politic. The college's members gather in libraries and sometimes in actual colleges, complete with classrooms and dormitories, to share their lore with one another. They also meet at festivals or affairs of state, where they can expose corruption, unravel lies, and poke fun at self-important figures of authority.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: When you join the College of Lore at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

features.name: Cutting Words
description: Also at 3rd level, you learn how to use your wit to distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.

When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll.

You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the GM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage. The creature is immune if it can't hear you or if it's immune to being charmed.

features.name: Additional Magical Secrets
description: At 6th level, you learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, as shown on the Bard table, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

features.name: Peerless Skill
description: Starting at 14th level, when you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the GM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

subclasses.name: Open Hand
description: Monks of the Way of the Open Hand are the ultimate masters of martial arts combat, whether armed or unarmed. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents, manipulate ki to heal damage to their bodies, and practice advanced meditation that can protect them from harm.

features.name: Open Hand Technique
description: Starting when you choose this tradition at 3rd level, you can manipulate your enemy's ki when you harness your own. Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone.
- It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you.
- It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Wholeness of Body
description: At 6th level, you gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

features.name: Tranquility
description: Beginning at 11th level, you can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.

features.name: Quivering Palm
description: At 17th level, you gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. To do so, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage.
You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can choose to end the vibrations harmlessly without using an action.

subclasses.name: Thief
description: You hone your skills in the larcenous arts. Burglars, bandits, cutpurses, and other criminals typically follow this archetype, but so do rogues who prefer to think of themselves as professional treasure seekers, explorers, delvers, and investigators. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you learn skills useful for delving into ancient ruins, reading unfamiliar languages, and using magic items you normally couldn't employ.

features.name: Fast Hands
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

features.name: Second-Story Work
description: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.
In addition, when you make a running jump, the distance you cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Dexterity modifier.

features.name: Supreme Sneak
description: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

features.name: Use Magic Device
description: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of magic that you can improvise the use of items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of magic items.

features.name: Thief's Reflexes
description: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.

subclasses.name: Totem Warrior
description: The Path of the Totem Warrior is a spiritual journey, as the barbarian accepts a spirit animal as guide, protector, and inspiration. In battle, your totem spirit fills you with supernatural might, adding magical fuel to your barbarian rage.

features.name: Spirit Seeker
description: Yours is a path that seeks attunement with the natural world, granting you a kinship with beasts. At 3rd level when you adopt this path, you gain the ability to cast the beast sense and speak with animals spells, but only as rituals.

features.name: Totem Spirit
description: At 3rd level, when you adopt this path, you choose a totem spirit and gain a totem feature. You must make or acquire a physical totem object — an amulet or similar adornment — that incorporates fur or feathers, claws, teeth, or bones of the animal you choose. At your option, you also gain minor physical attributes from your totem animal. Your choices and the associated benefits are:
Bear. While raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage.
Eagle. While raging, other creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attacks against you, and you can use the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn.
Wolf. While raging, your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that is hostile to you.

features.name: Aspect of the Beast
description: At 6th level, you gain a magical benefit based on the totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one.
Bear. You gain the might of a bear. Your carrying capacity (including load, lift, and push) is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects.

Eagle. You gain the eyesight of an eagle. You can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks.
Wolf. You gain the hunting sensibilities of a wolf. You can track other creatures while traveling at a brisk pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace.

features.name: Spirit Walker
description: At 10th level, you can cast the commune with nature spell, but only as a ritual. When you do so, a spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast makes itself known to you and appears somewhere on the land you are in.

features.name: Totemic Attunement
description: At 14th level, you gain a magical benefit based on a totem animal you choose. You can choose the same animal you chose at 3rd level or a different one.

Bear. While raging, any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you or another character with this feature. An enemy is immune to this effect if it can't see or hear you or if it can't be frightened.
Eagle. While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current speed. This benefit works only in short bursts; you fall if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.
Wolf. While raging, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock a Large or smaller creature prone when you hit it with a melee weapon attack.

subclasses.name: Valor
description: Bards of the College of Valor are daring skalds, telling tales of great heroes and performing deeds worthy of song.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

features.name: Combat Inspiration
description: Also at 3rd level, you learn to inspire others in combat. A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it hits or misses.

features.name: Extra Attack
description: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Battle Magic
description: At 14th level, you have mastered the art of weaving spellcasting and weapon use together. When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Knowledge
description: The Knowledge domain represents the pursuit of knowledge and understanding of the world and the gods.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
description: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice and gain two skills of your choice.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to tap into a reservoir of knowledge.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to read minds.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Visions of the Past
description: Starting at 17th level, you can call upon your deity to reveal visions of the past.

subclasses.name: Light
description: The Light domain represents the power of light, fire, and revelation.

features.name: Bonus Cantrip
description: At 1st level, you gain the light cantrip if you don't already know it.

features.name: Radiance of the Dawn
description: Starting at 1st level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be blinded or deafened.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to flood an area with radiant energy.

features.name: Improved Flare
description: Starting at 6th level, you can cast the fireball spell once per long rest.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Corona of Light
description: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to emanate a bright light.

subclasses.name: Nature
description: The Nature domain represents the power of the natural world.

features.name: Acolyte of Nature
description: At 1st level, you learn one druid cantrip of your choice.

features.name: Nature's Savagery
description: At 1st level, you gain the ability to channel divine power to damage a creature.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to charm animals and plants.

features.name: Dampen Elements
description: Starting at 6th level, you can use your reaction to reduce damage.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Master of Nature
description: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to charm beasts and plants.

subclasses.name: Tempest
description: The Tempest domain represents the power of storms and the sea.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: Wrath of the Storm
description: Also at 1st level, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to a creature within 5 feet of you.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to maximize the damage of your lightning or thunder spells.

features.name: Thunderbolt Strike
description: Starting at 6th level, when you deal lightning damage to a creature, you can push it up to 10 feet away.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Stormborn
description: Starting at 17th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage.

subclasses.name: Trickery
description: The Trickery domain represents the power of deception and illusion.

features.name: Blessing of the Trickster
description: At 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to create an illusory duplicate of yourself.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to become invisible.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Divine Strike
description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with poison.

features.name: Improved Duplicity
description: At 17th level, you can create more than one illusory duplicate.

subclasses.name: War
description: The War domain represents the power of battle and conflict.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
description: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

features.name: War Priest
description: Also at 1st level, you can make a bonus action attack when you use the Attack action.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
description: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to add +10 to an attack roll.

features.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
description: At 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity to grant resistance to an ally.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
description: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage rolls of your cleric spells.

features.name: Avatar of Battle
description: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subclasses.name: Moon
description: Druids of the Circle of the Moon are fierce guardians of the natural order.

features.name: Combat Wild Shape
description: At 2nd level, you can use Wild Shape as a bonus action.

features.name: Circle Forms
description: Also at 2nd level, you can transform into more powerful beasts.

features.name: Primal Strike
description: Starting at 6th level, your attacks in beast form count as magical.

features.name: Elemental Wild Shape
description: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Wild Shape to transform into an elemental.

features.name: Thousand Forms
description: At 14th level, you can cast the alter self spell at will.

subclasses.name: Battle Master
description: Battle Masters are commanders who study the art of war and use maneuvers to control the battlefield.

features.name: Combat Superiority
description: At 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by superiority dice.

features.name: Student of War
description: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one skill and one tool.

features.name: Know Your Enemy
description: Starting at 7th level, you can assess a creature's capabilities.

features.name: Relentless
description: At 15th level, you regain a superiority die on a roll of 1.

subclasses.name: Eldritch Knight
description: Eldritch Knights are fighters who combine martial prowess with arcane magic.

features.name: Spellcasting
description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells.

features.name: Weapon Bond
description: Also at 3rd level, you can bond with a weapon.

features.name: War Magic
description: At 7th level, you can cast a spell and attack as a bonus action.

features.name: Eldritch Strike
description: At 10th level, you can impose disadvantage on a creature's saving throws against your spells.

features.name: Arcane Charge
description: At 15th level, you can teleport as part of your Action Surge.

features.name: Improved War Magic
description: At 18th level, you can cast a spell and attack twice as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Shadow
description: Monks of the Way of Shadow follow the path of darkness and stealth.

features.name: Shadow Arts
description: At 3rd level, you can use ki to replicate certain spells.

features.name: Shadow Step
description: Starting at 6th level, you can teleport as a bonus action.

features.name: Cloak of Shadows
description: At 11th level, you can become invisible as a bonus action.

features.name: Opportunist
description: At 17th level, you can make an opportunity attack when a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack.

subclasses.name: Four Elements
description: Monks of the Way of the Four Elements harness the power of the elements.

features.name: Disciple of the Elements
description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to manipulate the four elements.

features.name: Elemental Attunement
description: Also at 3rd level, you can use ki to cast spells.

features.name: Elemental Discipline
description: At 6th level, you gain additional elemental disciplines.

features.name: Everlasting Flame
description: At 11th level, you have resistance to fire damage.

features.name: Sweeping Cinder Strike
description: At 11th level, you can create a wave of fire.

subclasses.name: Ancients
description: The Oath of the Ancients represents the power of nature and the fey.

features.name: Oath Spells
description: At 3rd level, you gain oath spells.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Nature's Wrath
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to ensnare a creature.

features.name: Aura of Warding
description: Starting at 7th level, you gain resistance to spell damage.

features.name: Undying Sentinel
description: At 15th level, you can't be reduced below 1 hit point.

features.name: Elder Champion
description: At 20th level, you can transform into an ancient being.

subclasses.name: Vengeance
description: The Oath of Vengeance represents the power of righteous fury and retribution.

features.name: Oath Spells
description: At 3rd level, you gain oath spells.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Abjure Enemy
description: Starting at 3rd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to frighten a creature.

features.name: Relentless Avenger
description: At 7th level, you can move when you hit a creature with an opportunity attack.

features.name: Soul of Vengeance
description: At 15th level, you can cast hold monster on a creature you have damaged.

features.name: Avenging Angel
description: At 20th level, you can transform into an avenging angel.

subclasses.name: Beast Master
description: Rangers of the Beast Master form a bond with a beast companion.

features.name: Ranger's Companion
description: At 3rd level, you gain a beast companion.

features.name: Exceptional Training
description: Starting at 7th level, your beast companion can take actions on your turn.

features.name: Bestial Fury
description: At 11th level, your beast companion can attack twice.

features.name: Share Spells
description: At 15th level, you can cast spells on your beast companion.

subclasses.name: Assassin
description: Assassins are killers who strike from the shadows.

features.name: Assassinate
description: At 3rd level, you are at your deadliest when you get the drop on your enemies.

features.name: Infiltrator
description: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with disguise kit and forgery kit.

features.name: Impostor
description: At 9th level, you can mimic speech and handwriting.

features.name: Death Strike
description: At 17th level, you become a master of death.

subclasses.name: Arcane Trickster
description: Arcane Tricksters are rogues who blend magic with stealth.

features.name: Spellcasting
description: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
description: Also at 3rd level, you can make your mage hand invisible.

features.name: Magical Ambush
description: At 9th level, you can impose disadvantage on saving throws against your spells.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
description: At 13th level, you can use your bonus action to distract a creature.

features.name: Spell Thief
description: At 17th level, you can steal a spell from a creature.

subclasses.name: Wild Magic
description: Wild Magic sorcerers are born with chaotic magic that surges within them.

features.name: Wild Magic Surge
description: At 1st level, you can roll on the Wild Magic Surge table after casting a spell.

features.name: Tides of Chaos
description: Also at 1st level, you can gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

features.name: Bend Luck
description: At 6th level, you can manipulate fate.

features.name: Controlled Chaos
description: At 14th level, you can roll twice on the Wild Magic Surge table.

features.name: Spell Bombardment
description: At 18th level, your spells deal extra damage.

subclasses.name: Great Old One
description: The Great Old One is a mysterious and ancient entity from beyond the stars.

features.name: Awakened Mind
description: At 1st level, you can communicate telepathically.

features.name: Entropic Ward
description: At 6th level, you can impose disadvantage on an attack roll against you.

features.name: Thought Shield
description: At 10th level, you have resistance to psychic damage.

features.name: Create Thrall
description: At 14th level, you can charm a creature.

subclasses.name: Undying
description: The Undying represent those who have made pacts with powerful undead beings.

features.name: Among the Dead
description: At 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against being frightened.

features.name: Undying Nature
description: Also at 1st level, you have advantage on saving throws against disease.

features.name: Beyond the Grave
description: At 6th level, you can gain temporary hit points when you finish a short rest.

features.name: Indestructible Life
description: At 10th level, you can regain hit points when you take damage.

features.name: Undying Nature
description: At 14th level, you can't be killed by a single attack.

subclasses.name: Abjuration
description: Abjuration wizards focus on protective and defensive magic.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an abjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Arcane Ward
description: Also at 2nd level, you can create a magical ward.

features.name: Projected Ward
description: At 6th level, you can use your Arcane Ward to protect others.

features.name: Resilient Ward
description: At 10th level, your Arcane Ward regains hit points when you finish a short rest.

features.name: Spell Resistance
description: At 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against spells.

subclasses.name: Conjuration
description: Conjuration wizards specialize in creating objects and creatures from nothing.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a conjuration spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Conjuration
description: Also at 2nd level, you can conjure small objects.

features.name: Benign Transposition
description: At 6th level, you can swap places with a creature.

features.name: Focused Conjuration
description: At 10th level, your concentration on conjuration spells is not broken when you take damage.

features.name: Durable Summons
description: At 14th level, your summoned creatures gain temporary hit points.

subclasses.name: Divination
description: Divination wizards study the art of predicting the future.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a divination spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Portent
description: Also at 2nd level, you can replace any attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.

features.name: Expert Divination
description: At 6th level, you can regain spell slots when you cast divination spells.

features.name: Third Eye
description: At 10th level, you can gain darkvision, see invisible creatures, etc.

features.name: Future Sight
description: At 14th level, you can cast the foresight spell once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Enchantment
description: Enchantment wizards specialize in manipulating the minds of others.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an enchantment spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Hypnotic Gaze
description: Also at 2nd level, you can charm a creature with a look.

features.name: Instinctive Charm
description: At 6th level, you can divert attacks made against you.

features.name: Split Enchantment
description: At 10th level, you can target two creatures with enchantment spells.

features.name: Alter Memories
description: At 14th level, you can modify a creature's memory.

subclasses.name: Illusion
description: Illusion wizards create false images and manipulate perceptions.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy an illusion spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Malleable Illusion
description: Also at 2nd level, you can change the nature of your illusions.

features.name: Illusory Self
description: At 6th level, you can create an illusory duplicate of yourself.

features.name: Illusory Reality
description: At 10th level, you can make an illusion real.

features.name: Illusory Being
description: At 14th level, you can create an illusory creature.

subclasses.name: Necromancy
description: Necromancy wizards study the forces of life and death.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a necromancy spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Grim Harvest
description: Also at 2nd level, you can regain hit points when you kill a creature.

features.name: Undead Thralls
description: At 6th level, you can animate undead.

features.name: Inured to Undeath
description: At 10th level, you have resistance to necrotic damage.

features.name: Command Undead
description: At 14th level, you can command undead creatures.

subclasses.name: Transmutation
description: Transmutation wizards manipulate the physical world.

features.name: Savant
description: At 2nd level, the gold and time you spend to copy a transmutation spell into your spellbook is halved.

features.name: Minor Alchemy
description: Also at 2nd level, you can transmute materials.

features.name: Transmuter's Stone
description: At 6th level, you can create a stone that grants benefits.

features.name: Shapechanger
description: At 10th level, you can cast the polymorph spell on yourself.

features.name: Master Transmuter
description: At 14th level, you can transmute matter at a touch.
